newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan bourse reforms set to ease restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Milan bourse reforms set to ease restrictions.

text.p: Reforms to the Italian stock market under the new Eurosim regulations will ease restrictions placed on professional and private investors, according to draft rules from market watchdog authority Consob.
The outline proposals will mean that the principle of concentrating trade within the Milan stock exchange does not apply to qualified investors such as banks, investment companies, and brokers.
The current rule stipulating the minimum number of lots for off-bourse trading such as block trades will be less binding, according to the draft rules.

For private investors, the draft rules see the possibility of operating outside the bourse only when the investor is authorized and the investor agrees to carry out the best execution for its clients. Consob underlines that the text is not the final version and all interested parties will have until September 20 to express their opinions.
Financial sources noted that the guiding principle of concentrating trade on the bourse introduced by a law on Sims in 1991 remains valid within the few limits allowed by the Eurosim directive.
